objective: Select the next measured workstream after closing the policy-selected filelist repeat-median public-pack externalization boundary.

decision.reason: The sidecar workflow now has scoped filelist-derived correctness, timing, policy-selected 64x1 repeat-median evidence, and public-pack closure. The next useful gap is defining the smallest native-Verilator-option prototype boundary that can reuse this sidecar evidence without claiming arbitrary RTL support, hidden dependency inference, or automatic optimal GPU allocation.

candidate_review.reason: It directly addresses the operator goal of making hybrid execution as simple as a Verilator option while keeping the first prototype explicitly scoped to reviewed sidecar inputs.
The policy-selected repeat-median result covers two reviewed filelist-derived targets at 64x1; it is not enough to claim automatic optimum selection for arbitrary filelists.
Dependency inference is an input-closure problem and should not be hidden behind a native-option prototype.
Resident execution targets repeated-step weakness, while the selected policy evidence is state-parallel 64x1.
GEM comparison should wait until the user-facing option boundary is explicit enough to compare fairly.
